skills.name: The basics of a developed essay

note.text: An introduction establishes subject and direction. A body paragraph develops a focused point with explanation or examples and connects it to the overall purpose. Connectors express actual relations such as contrast or cause; inserting however randomly does not create one. A conclusion draws the answer together without introducing an unrelated major claim. No fixed sentence count guarantees quality.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to develop a controlling idea through connected paragraphs and a purposeful conclusion. Builds on: essay purpose and planning. Leads to: reading dialogue and directed writing.

paper_task.prompt: Develop your outline into an essay explaining clearer school messages. Include an introduction, developed body paragraphs and conclusion. Follow the teacher’s required length; the model illustrates development, not a compulsory word count.
model: A notice helps only when readers can work out what action is expected. A heading may attract attention, but the details must also be clear. Improving a club notice requires a recognisable purpose, useful information and a way to confirm uncertain details.

First, a precise heading identifies the activity. Reading club discussion tells a reader more than Important! The body should explain who is invited and what preparation is needed. Such details connect the heading to an action rather than leaving the audience to guess.

A notice also needs honest treatment of uncertainty. If a room is unconfirmed, presenting it as settled may mislead readers. The writer can mark it provisional and identify whom to ask. Clear wording cannot make an uncertain arrangement certain, but it can show what remains to be checked.
A useful notice combines a focused heading with checked details. Its value lies in helping readers understand their next step, not in filling a page with impressive words.
checklist: Introduction: an opening establishing topic and direction.
Developed paragraph: a focused point supported by explanation.
Logical connection: a link expressing an actual relationship.
Conclusion: an ending drawing together the developed answer.
Use relevant original details and check sentence boundaries, agreement and spelling.
